grade.primary_choice: Keep it in Ruby: a dedicated webhook queue and ECS service autoscaled on queue latency, then per-endpoint isolation
grade.notes: The answer covers all seven must-mention points: Little's law capacity math, GVL release during I/O, head-of-line blocking with per-endpoint caps and circuit breakers, a dedicated queue autoscaled on latency, payloads built up front to keep Postgres connections out of the send path, and a concrete measurement plan, with Go kept as a later option. Its technical details (Net::HTTP 60 s defaults, 25 Sidekiq retries, the noeviction requirement, the ECS metadata addresses) are accurate; the one gap is that the SaaS option mentions pricing but not data-handling or compliance review.
